limitations: The deleted remote release asset was unavailable for rescanning.
CodeQL and dependency review require a GitHub-hosted workflow run before they are verified.
Bastet was explicitly authorized and exercised as an upgrade target; no clean external-user host, unrelated LAN source, SMTP server, or webhook receiver was contacted.

findings.title: Human control-plane routes lacked authentication
findings.root_cause: The operator API had no server-side identity or session boundary.
findings.impact: A reachable client could read operational data, mutate configuration, and start costly operations.
findings.remediation: Added fail-closed middleware, a signed HttpOnly session, Bearer support, CSRF validation, expiry, login throttling, and strict browser headers.

findings.title: Remote agent accepted requests without a configured or strong token
findings.root_cause: Missing authentication configuration was treated as an opt-out and weak tokens were accepted.
findings.impact: A reachable agent could expose telemetry or execute model/eval actions without adequate authentication.
findings.remediation: Missing or shorter-than-32-character tokens now fail closed with HTTP 503; new installs reject weak tokens.

findings.title: Integration automation accepted requests without a configured token
findings.root_cause: Missing external API authentication was treated as an opt-out and one route omitted the dependency.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated imports, exports, reports, inventory, email, or webhook dispatch could be reached.
findings.remediation: Every automation route now fails closed and requires a distinct key of at least 32 characters.

findings.title: Webhook dispatch allowed unrestricted targets and retained secret URLs
findings.root_cause: An empty allowlist allowed any HTTP(S) destination, resolved address classes were unchecked, redirects were allowed, and complete URLs were persisted.
findings.impact: SSRF against local/private/metadata services and disclosure of signed webhook URL paths.
findings.remediation: Required an exact authority allowlist, validated resolved addresses, disabled redirects, made private networks opt-in, applied timeouts, and redacted URLs.

findings.title: Docker ports defaulted to every host interface
findings.root_cause: Published ports omitted the host address.
findings.impact: Network peers could reach application services unintentionally.
findings.remediation: Defaulted published ports to 127.0.0.1 and removed the production backend publication.
regression_evidence: docker compose ps reports only 127.0.0.1 publishers

findings.title: Frontend development dependency graph contained known vulnerabilities
findings.root_cause: The lockfile selected vulnerable build and test dependencies.
findings.remediation: Updated the lock graph within declared compatible versions.

findings.title: CI used an EOL runtime, mutable Actions, and overbroad publication credentials
findings.root_cause: Node 20, mutable action tags, and combined build/publication permissions expanded supply-chain risk.
findings.impact: Unsupported build runtime and avoidable workflow-token exposure.
findings.remediation: Moved to Node 24, pinned every Action to a full SHA, defaulted permissions to read-only, and isolated write-token publication.

findings.title: Release bundles copied untracked cache and bytecode artifacts
findings.root_cause: Recursive directory copies included local untracked content.
findings.impact: Release contamination, stale code, local metadata, or secret leakage.
findings.remediation: Release inputs now come only from git ls-files.
regression_evidence: 149-entry smoke ZIP: 0 forbidden entries and 0 required entries missing

findings.title: Production containers ran as root
findings.root_cause: Production images did not declare unprivileged runtime users.
findings.impact: A container compromise would have broader filesystem and process impact.
findings.remediation: Added unprivileged users, unprivileged frontend port, read-only filesystems, tmpfs mounts, dropped capabilities, and no-new-privileges.
regression_evidence: production health checks and proxy passed

findings.title: Costly AI and evaluation routes lacked global abuse bounds
findings.root_cause: Authenticated callers could initiate costly work without shared rate, concurrency, input, or output limits.
findings.impact: Resource exhaustion, unexpected model cost, and oversized stored or returned data.
findings.remediation: Added bounded rate/concurrency leases plus prompt, suite, description, output-token, and response-size caps.

findings.title: Dependency resolution could select a vulnerable idna release
findings.root_cause: The transitive dependency had no safe direct lower bound in standalone installation manifests.
findings.impact: A fresh installation could resolve an affected package version.
findings.remediation: Added idna>=3.15 to both dependency manifests.
regression_evidence: final backend image: 0 fixed HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities

findings.title: Linux agent onboarding exposed the shared secret to shell history and defaulted to bearer authentication
findings.root_cause: The documented install command accepted the long-lived shared agent token inline and new-install examples selected bearer mode.
findings.impact: Operators following the guide could retain a fleet-wide agent credential in shell history, while bearer requests lacked replay protection.
findings.remediation: The installer now prompts interactively, validates URL-safe entropy, defaults new installs to HMAC, and the public workflows no longer place secrets in commands.

findings.title: Interactive remote model requests bypassed the HMAC-aware transport
findings.root_cause: Polling used the signed client while capability checks and eval paths independently constructed bearer-only headers.
findings.impact: A correctly configured HMAC agent failed closed for interactive and scheduled model work, leaving the documented stronger-auth workflow incomplete.
findings.remediation: All remote agent paths now share one transport that signs the exact serialized body and maps authentication failures consistently.
regression_evidence: isolated HMAC setup check reported status=ok and matching node_id
